grades.question: How is the Conflict deck built, and what happens to unused Conflict cards?
grades.expected: Shuffle all four III cards at the bottom, five randomly dealt of nine II cards above, one randomly dealt of three I cards on top: ten total. Return unused cards to the box without looking.

observed.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle all 9 II cards and deal 5 face down above them; shuffle all 3 I cards and deal 1 face down on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box without looking at them.
observed.evidence: Setup: face-down 10-card Conflict Deck; shuffle each entire tier before dealing.

grades.reason: Both specify shuffled 4 III / 5 of 9 II / 1 of 3 I in order, face down, with unused cards returned unseen.

grades.question: What are the starting score, Agents, troops and water for a human in a four-player game versus a three-player game?
grades.expected: Four players start at 1 VP; three at 0. Each has two Agents on Leader and third beside board, three troops in garrison with remaining nine in supply, and one water.

observed.answer: A human starts at 1 VP in a four-player game and 0 VP in a three-player game. Both setups give 2 Agents on the Leader and the Swordmaster beside the board, 12 troops total with 3 in the garrison and 9 in supply, and 1 water.
observed.evidence: Setup step 6: Score marker on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents; 3 troops in garrison, 9 in supply; take 1 water.

grades.reason: Each distinguishes four-player 1 VP from three-player 0 and supplies all Agent, troop and water quantities and locations.

grades.question: Can you Reveal with Agents left, and can you later take an Agent turn in the same round? What cards supply Reveal effects and where do all played cards go?
grades.expected: May Reveal early; no more turns this phase after Reveal. Only cards remaining in hand and just revealed supply Reveal effects, not Agent-turn cards. Clean Up puts all Agent and Reveal cards in discard pile.

observed.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents, and after Revealing you are skipped for the rest of Player Turns, so cannot take another Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed in the Reveal step, not Agent-turn cards. At Clean Up, move all cards in front of you from both kinds of turns to your discard pile.
observed.evidence: Player Turns; Reveal Turn: resolve Reveal boxes of just-revealed cards; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to discard.

grades.reason: Each permits early Reveal, bars subsequent Agent turns, limits Reveal effects to just-revealed hand cards, and discards both groups.

grades.question: May an Agent-turn card effect provide resources to pay the destination entry cost? How many Agents can one card send, and can a card without Agent icons be used?
grades.expected: Entry costs paid immediately before any card or space effects; cannot use later gains to pay entry. One card sends one Agent using one matching icon. No-icon card cannot be played on an Agent turn.

observed.answer: A Plot Intrigue played before placing the Agent may grant resources that are then available for the entry cost. Resources from the played Agent card or destination, which occur only after placement, cannot pay that same cost. One card sends one Agent using one of its icons; it cannot send multiple Agents. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn.
observed.evidence: Player Turns entry-cost timing; Agent Turn: choose only one Agent icon; no Agent icons means Reveal only.

grades.reason: Each bars post-placement card/space gains from entry payment and states one Agent/one icon and no-icon prohibition; pre-entry Plot exception is supported.

grades.question: At a Combat space you recruit three troops this turn and already have four garrisoned. How many can deploy? What if the destination is not a Combat space, and where do recruited troops originate?
grades.expected: May deploy all three newly recruited plus at most two older garrison troops, five total. Normal deployment unavailable at noncombat space. Recruit from own supply into garrison; empty supply prevents recruiting.

observed.answer: At a Combat space, you may deploy all 3 troops recruited this turn plus up to 2 from the garrison, for 5 total. At a non-Combat space you do not deploy troops. Recruited troops come from your supply into your garrison; if supply is empty you cannot recruit more.
observed.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying Units: newly recruited this turn plus up to two from garrison, at a Combat space; cube recruits from supply to garrison.

grades.reason: Each gives five as three new plus two older troops, limits normal deployment to Combat spaces and identifies supply-to-garrison recruitment.

grades.question: How do you use a Spy Agent icon, Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence? Can the same Spy pay for both, and when must Gather Intelligence be chosen?
grades.expected: Spy Agent icon permits a connected space without recalling Spy. Infiltrate recalls own connected Spy to bypass another player Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls own connected Spy to draw, chosen immediately after placement before card/space effects. Same Spy cannot do both; separate Spies can.

observed.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets an Agent go to any space connected to one of your Spy-occupied observation posts without recalling that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy at a connected post to bypass another player's Agent on the destination; it cannot bypass your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy after Agent placement and before any space or card effects to draw a card. The same Spy cannot pay for both; you may use two different Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence. Choose Gather Intelligence immediately after placing the Agent.
observed.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy Agent icon; Infiltrate; Gather Intelligence timing; cannot recall same Spy for both.

grades.reason: Each distinguishes non-recalling Spy-icon access from recalling for Infiltrate or a draw, gives placement-before-effects draw timing, and requires separate Spies.

grades.question: With two troops, one sandworm and four revealed swords, what is your strength? What if your final unit is removed? Can you participate in Combat Intrigue with no unit?
grades.expected: Strength 11 (2+2+3+4). No units means zero strength regardless swords. Without a unit cannot participate in Combat Intrigue.

observed.answer: Strength is 2 troops × 2 = 4, plus 1 sandworm × 3 = 3, plus 4 swords = 11. If your last unit is removed, strength becomes 0. You cannot play Combat Intrigue without at least one unit in the Conflict.
observed.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, revealed sword 1; need at least one unit. Intrigue cards: Combat only with a unit deployed.

grades.reason: Each computes 11, reduces strength to zero without units and disallows Combat Intrigue without a unit.

grades.question: If you pass Combat Intrigue and an opponent then plays one, may you act again? When does the window close, and where do troops and sandworms go after rewards?
grades.expected: May act again after earlier pass; closes only when all involved players pass consecutively. Adjust strength for effects. After all rewards troops return to supply not garrison, sandworms to bank, Combat markers reset zero.

observed.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you acting again after an opponent plays; the window closes when all players involved pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison) and sandworms return to the bank.
observed.evidence: Phase 3 Combat: players may play or pass; not required to pass just because passed earlier; all pass consecutively closes. Cleanup destinations stated.

grades.reason: Each permits acting after a pass, closes on consecutive passes and returns troops to supply and sandworms to bank; marker reset is unasked background.

grades.question: Compare two players tied for first in a four-player Conflict with the same tie in a three-player Conflict. Who takes the Conflict card, and can a zero-strength player get a reward?
grades.expected: Each tied first gets second reward and nobody wins or takes card. In four-player game remaining players compete for third; in three-player game no further rewards. Zero strength never rewarded.

observed.answer: With two tied for first in four-player play, each receives the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward, and nobody takes the Conflict card. The same first-place tie in a three-player game gives each tied player the second reward, with no other reward; nobody takes the card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
observed.evidence: Resolve Combat and Conflict ties by player count; 0 strength receives no reward.

grades.reason: Each gives both tied-first players second reward, no card, four-player remaining competition for third versus no other three-player reward, and zero-strength exclusion.

grades.question: What does a sandworm do to rewards: do two sandworms quadruple them, can control or battle icons double, and how is a reward offering 3 spice for 1 VP handled?
grades.expected: One or more sandworms doubles, never quadruples. Control and battle icons do not double. Optional reward cost may be paid second time: 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 for 2, not free second VP.

observed.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards; two worms do not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on won Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For an optional reward of 1 VP for 3 spice, you may pay a second 3 spice for a second VP (6 spice total for 2 VP).
observed.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more doubles; location control and battle icons excluded; optional cost may be paid again.

grades.reason: Each doubles once for any positive sandworm count, excludes control/battle icons and requires another 3 spice for the second VP.

grades.question: When is a normal battle-icon match checked, which cards qualify, is matching optional, and how is a wild icon used?
grades.expected: After winning and taking Conflict card face up in supply check another face-up Conflict or Objective with same icon; must flip pair face down for 1 VP. At Endgame wild can match any of three icons in supply, pair flipped for 1 VP.

observed.answer: After you win and take the Conflict card face up into your supply, check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card there. A matching icon pair must be flipped face down for 1 VP; matching is mandatory. At Endgame, the wild icon may match any one of the three battle icons in your supply, flipping the pair for 1 VP.
observed.evidence: Battle Icons; winner's card procedure orders taking card first, then checking mandatory match.

grades.reason: Each places the normal check after taking the won card, uses face-up Conflict/Objective pairs mandatorily for 1 VP and confines wild matching to Endgame.

grades.question: What are the rewards and reversibility at 2 and 4 Faction Influence, and does tying the Alliance holder at 4 steal the Alliance?
grades.expected: Reach 2 gets 1 VP lost below 2. Reach 4 gets track bonus retained if falling below, can earn again on re-reaching. First to 4 gets Alliance and its VP; tie does not steal, opponent must rise higher. Transfer loses old holder VP and gives new holder VP.

observed.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses it, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if you later fall below 4 and earned again on returning to 4; the first player to 4 also takes the Alliance and its 1 VP. Tying the current holder does not steal the Alliance; you must rise above their Influence. The Alliance VP follows its holder and transfers away if lost.
observed.evidence: Victory Points: Faction Influence; retained track bonus versus temporary Alliance VP; tie does not steal.

grades.reason: Each explains reversible 2-Influence VP, retained/re-earnable 4-track bonus, Alliance VP transfer and no theft on a challenger tie.

grades.question: When can Persuasion be spent during Reveal, may it be pooled or split, can you buy a Row replacement immediately, and where does the acquired card go?
grades.expected: Before between or after Reveal effects; can pool and split. Refill Row to five immediately; may buy replacement with remaining Persuasion. Acquired card face-up discard, cannot use immediately; unspent Persuasion lost.

You may pool Persuasion from sources for one purchase and split one source among purchases; unused Persuasion is lost. Buy Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card at its top-right cost. After a Row purchase, replace it from the Imperium Deck and you may buy the replacement if able. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
observed.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Reveal turn purchases, timing, pooling/splitting, replacement, destination, unused Persuasion lost.

grades.reason: Each gives all spending windows, pooling/splitting, immediate replacement purchase and face-up discard destination; immediate use is unasked background.

grades.question: How do Maker bonus spice, the Shield Wall and Maker Hooks affect harvesting and summoning, and where can a sandworm be placed?
grades.expected: Makers phase adds one bonus spice on each unoccupied Maker space, accumulating; visiting collects all bonus spice. Shield Wall blocks worms at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, Imperial Basin until removed to box. Maker Hooks prerequisite when specified; summoning directly bank to Conflict, never garrison.

Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two worms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Hooks are required only when the summoning effect specifies them and are retained, not spent. A worm can never go in a garrison; Shield Wall prevents summoning to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin until removed.
observed.evidence: Phase 4 Makers; Sandworms and Sandworm Reward Doubling; board-space table: Deep Desert, Hagga Basin.

grades.reason: The answer covers Maker accumulation/collection, Hooks conditions and Wall protection, but gives only prohibited placement and protected locations; it never affirmatively says a summoned sandworm is immediately placed into the Conflict.

grades.question: At what point does 10 VP or an empty Conflict deck end play, what happens before comparing final VP, and what are the rulebook resource tiebreakers?
grades.expected: Check in Recall at end of round, not immediately at 10 VP. Resolve Endgame Intrigue first then highest VP wins. Ties spice then Solari then water then garrisoned troops.

observed.answer: Endgame triggers at the end of a round if anyone has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Players first resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards, then compare VP. Tiebreakers in order are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
observed.evidence: Phase 5 Recall; Scoring / Victory Conditions.

grades.reason: Each checks at round-end Recall, resolves Endgame Intrigue before comparing VP and gives spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops in order.

grades.question: With optional standard CHOAM, how many contracts start face up and face down, which extra cards are added, is Shaddam compulsory, and are the 10 contrasting-back contracts part of this standard setup?
grades.expected: 20 standard contracts: two face up, eighteen in bank. Add four Intrigue and four Imperium; Shaddam optional. Ten contrasting-back contracts are only Rise of Ix compatibility, excluded from standard setup.

observed.answer: Standard CHOAM setup shuffles the 20 standard contracts and exposes 2 face up, leaving 18 face down in the bank. Shuffle 4 additional Intrigue cards into the Intrigue Deck and 4 additional Imperium cards into the Imperium Deck. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts are left out; they are not part of the 20 standard tokens.
observed.evidence: CHOAM Module setup changes; contrasting-back contracts are separate Rise of Ix compatibility set.

grades.reason: Each gives the standard no-Shaddam two-up/eighteen-down distribution, adds four cards to each deck, makes Shaddam optional and excludes the ten Ix tokens; B also states the Shaddam setup exception.

grades.question: Under CHOAM, what does the contract icon do, what if all contracts are taken, and how are Harvest, Immediate and Acquire The Spice Must Flow contracts completed?
grades.expected: Take one of two face-up into supply then refill face up from bank; if all taken gain 2 Solari (also without module). Harvest: visit Maker and gain specified total spice that turn including other sources. Immediate upon taking. Acquire The Spice Must Flow on next acquiring that card.

observed.answer: With CHOAM and contracts available, the icon takes one of the two face-up contracts and replaces it with a face-up token from the bank; without CHOAM, or once all contracts have been taken, it gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining the stated spice total that turn; Immediate completes as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
observed.evidence: Taking contracts; Completing contracts; Human contract icon shared rule.

grades.reason: Each takes one of the two offered contracts and refills face up, gives the 2-Solari exhausted fallback and all three completion triggers; taking a contract contextually denotes possession in supply.

grades.question: You gain a board-space contract after already sending your Agent to that space this turn. Can you complete it now? Once completed what do you announce, gain and do with the token?
grades.expected: Cannot complete now; must have held contract when Agent sent, wait future turn. Announce completion, gain printed rewards, flip face down and leave in supply.

observed.answer: No. If you take a board-space contract for a space you already visited that turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must hold it when you send the Agent. On completion announce it, gain its rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
observed.evidence: Completing contracts: already visited space must wait; completion procedure.

grades.reason: Each disallows retroactive completion and gives announcement, rewards, face-down state and retained supply destination.

grades.question: In standard two-player play how many Rivals are used, who gets the Ornithopter Objective, who gets First Player, what is the turn order, and does a Rival Reveal?
grades.expected: One shared Rival. Rival gets Ornithopter Objective, other two randomly humans; Rival never First Player. Marker alternates humans, Rival considered clockwise from First Player and acts between humans each round. Takes Agent turns while it has Agent in supply, never Reveals.

It gets the Ornithopter Objective; eligible Objective cards are randomly dealt to the humans, and the human with the First Player marker on their Objective goes first. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival never Reveals.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: setup, turn order, Agent turns.

grades.reason: Each identifies one shared scoring Rival, its Ornithopter, human Objective-based First Player, intervening Rival turn and no Reveal; B also states later marker alternation.

grades.question: A Rival reveals an occupied board space, then a Place Spy card. How does it proceed, which space costs and effects apply, and what happens when House Hagal is empty or Reshuffle is drawn?
grades.expected: Occupied: ignore and reveal again. Place Spy tries empty designated post, ignore placement if none, then reveal another card regardless because no Agent sent. Ignore normal space costs/effects; use Hagal effects only. Empty deck or Reshuffle: immediately reshuffle Hagal and continue.

observed.answer: For an occupied indicated destination, ignore it and reveal another House Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: attempt an empty post of the specified type, ignore placement if none exists, then immediately reveal another card and continue the Agent turn. Ignore normal space costs and effects; apply only the Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
observed.evidence: Rival Agent turns; Place Spy cards; ignore normal space costs and effects.

grades.reason: Each redraws after occupied destinations, attempts specified Spy placement and redraws regardless, uses Hagal rather than ordinary costs/effects and immediately reshuffles as required.

grades.question: How are eligible Objective cards selected and distributed in standard three- or four-player setup, how is First Player chosen, and may Shaddam be chosen without CHOAM?
grades.expected: Omit Objectives whose 1–3P or 4/6P mark mismatches count; shuffle, each takes one random face up in supply. First Player is holder of marked Objective. Shaddam cannot be chosen without CHOAM.

observed.answer: In 3–4-player setup, omit Objectives with a player-count marking that does not match, shuffle the eligible cards, and give one face up to each player; the marked card determines First Player. Shaddam may be used only with the CHOAM Module, so not without it.
observed.evidence: Setup steps 3 and 5; Shaddam is used only with CHOAM.

grades.reason: Each removes mismatched count marks, shuffles/deals one face-up eligible Objective per human, uses marked Objective for First Player and excludes Shaddam without CHOAM.

grades.question: If the bank runs out of Solari, spice, water or sandworms, what happens? Contrast an empty personal troop supply, and state where resource payments go.
grades.expected: Bank resources and sandworms not limited; substitute conveniently. Cannot recruit troops from empty personal supply until returned. Resource gains come from bank and payments return to bank.

observed.answer: Solari, spice, and water are not limited: substitute conveniently if the bank runs out; the supply of sandworms is likewise not meant to be limited. Troops are limited by the personal supply: if it is empty, you cannot recruit until troops return there. Payments of Solari, spice, or water go back to the bank.
observed.evidence: Setup step 7: resources and sandworms not meant to be limited; payments return to bank. Recruiting & Deploying Units.

grades.reason: Each treats bank resources/sandworms as substitutable, personal troops as limited and returns payments to bank.

grades.question: State all five round phases in order, when Conflict and hand cards are drawn, and what Recall does if Endgame is not triggered.
grades.expected: Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. Start reveals top Conflict face up atop previous remaining cards then each draws five. If no Endgame, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise and begin next round (two-player Rival exception).

observed.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict card, resolve any defensive troop bonus, then each player draws 5 cards. At Recall, if Endgame is not triggered, humans return Agents to Leaders; with 3–4 humans pass First Player clockwise, or in two-player play return Rival Agents to its supply and pass First Player to the other human, then start the next round.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure: five phases; Phase 1; Phase 5 Recall.

grades.reason: Each gives all five phases in order, Round Start Conflict/hand timing and the full non-Endgame Recall procedure including two-player exception.

grades.question: May you resolve board-space effects, Agent-box effects and Faction Influence in any order? Can you use that visit’s Influence to meet its entry requirement?
grades.expected: Resolve effects in any order after placement, but entry requirements and costs must be met before any effects. Cannot rely on Influence gained by the visit for its entry requirement.

observed.evidence: Agent Turn: costs before resolving effects; effects may be in any order; Faction advance on Faction space.

grades.reason: Each separates freely ordered effects from pre-entry requirements and disallows the visit's own Influence for entry.

grades.question: Can an optional arrow cost be paid twice in an Agent turn? Which effects are normally optional or mandatory, including costs on Intrigue cards?
grades.expected: Only once per turn, except sandworm-doubled Conflict rewards. Most effects mandatory except may, optional arrow payment and black-X trash. Direct self-trash mandatory. All Intrigue conditions/costs required to play it.
grades.source_references: Main pp9,20; FAQ p3 optional effects/paying a cost

observed.evidence: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ & Rulings: Mandatory effects and costs.

grades.reason: Each prohibits repeating an Agent-turn arrow effect and distinguishes normally mandatory effects from may/arrow/black-X exceptions while requiring Intrigue costs; A states the Conflict-doubling exception and B expressly states mandatory self-trash.

grades.question: Where may a new Spy be placed, what if all your Spies are already deployed, and what if its placement effect specifies an Agent-icon type?
grades.expected: Unoccupied observation post, from supply. If none in supply may first recall one of own Spies for no effect. Specified icon must connect to post or cannot place there.

observed.answer: Place a Spy on an unoccupied observation post; if all your Spies are deployed, you may first recall one for no effect. If the placement effect requires a particular Agent-icon type connected to the post, the post must meet that requirement or you cannot place there.
observed.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy icon placement and specified Agent icon restrictions.

grades.question: Can you Infiltrate your own occupied board space, use a Spy without playing a card, or recall two connected Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement?
grades.expected: No to all. Infiltrate bypasses another player Agent; still play a card and meet entry costs/requirements. Two Spies can pay different effects (Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence), not duplicate Gather Intelligence.

Recalling a Spy for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence does not replace the need to play an appropriate card for an Agent turn. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; the same placement permits at most one Gather Intelligence, though another Spy may be used for Infiltrate.
observed.evidence: Spies & observation posts; FAQ Spies.

grades.reason: Each rejects self-Infiltration, cardless Agent turns and double Gather Intelligence, while permitting different Spies for different functions.

grades.question: Who gets control bonuses when visiting Arrakeen, Spice Refinery or Imperial Basin, how is control transferred, and where does the defensive troop originate?
grades.expected: Winning respective Conflict puts control marker on flag replacing opponent. Controller receives 1 Solari at Arrakeen/Refinery or 1 spice at Basin whenever anyone including self visits. Reveal of controlled location Conflict permits one troop from supply directly to Conflict.

A Conflict winner places/replaces the Control marker. When the Conflict for a controlled location is revealed, its controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict, without an Agent visit.
observed.evidence: Critical Locations & Control; Agent-turn defensive troop bonus; board-space table.

grades.reason: Each gives the controller's visit quantities including self-visits, transfers control on the corresponding Conflict win and deploys the defensive troop from supply.

grades.question: When two players tie for second in a three-player Conflict, what happens? What if players tie for third in four-player play, or three players tie for first?
grades.expected: Tied second each get third reward; winner keeps first and card, no other rewards. Tied third receive nothing. Three tied first each get second, no winner/card and no further rewards.

observed.answer: In a tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the first-place winner retains their reward and Conflict card, and there are no further rewards. Players tied for third get nothing. Three tied for first each get the second reward; nobody wins or takes the card and no other reward is given.
observed.evidence: Combat ties; Conflict ties by player count.

grades.reason: Each correctly resolves tied second, tied third and three tied first, including retained winner card and no further rewards.

grades.question: At a normal three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, which places receive rewards? What if a two-player game’s Rival is one of the participants?
grades.expected: Only first and second rewarded, third only used for a tie for second. Two humans plus standard Rival use the same two-/three-player reward rules; Rival competes normally.
grades.source_references: Main p14; Supplements p5 Combat; FAQ p1 Conflict

observed.answer: In a three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, first and second place receive their printed rewards; third gets nothing. This also applies in two-player play with a Rival, since that is a three-competitor game.
observed.evidence: Resolve Combat: with 2 or 3 players ordinary first and second receive rewards; third gets nothing unless tie for second.

grades.reason: Each pays ordinary first/second only and applies the same rule with a Rival; A's same-question evidence explicitly limits third reward to tied second.

grades.question: When can Plot, Combat and Endgame Intrigues be played, how are unplayed Intrigues kept and ordinary ones discarded, and what if the Intrigue deck is exhausted?
grades.expected: Plot during own Agent/Reveal turns, Combat during Combat with a unit, Endgame at game end. Unplayed face down separate from deck, owner may inspect; played resolved cards face up Intrigue discard. Exhaustion reshuffles Intrigue discard into new deck.
grades.source_references: Main p7 / extraction 345–354; FAQ p2 Intrigue cards

observed.answer: Plot Intrigue may be played during your Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigue only during Combat and only if you have a unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigue at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down, separate from your deck; after resolving one, place it face up in an Intrigue discard pile. If the Intrigue Deck runs out, shuffle its discard to form a new deck.
observed.evidence: Intrigue cards; FAQ Draw timing.

grades.reason: Each gives all three Intrigue windows and Combat eligibility, separate face-down storage, face-up discard and exhaustion reshuffle.

grades.question: Can you discard an Intrigue for an ordinary discard instruction? Where does an ordinary discard come from? How does Secrets choose which Intrigue is stolen?
grades.expected: Ordinary discard from hand and cannot be Intrigue unless specified. Secrets steals one random Intrigue from each opponent with four or more, in addition to drawing one from deck and gaining Bene Gesserit Influence.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1104–1106,1179–1181; Supplements p2; FAQ p2 discard

observed.answer: An ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand, and cannot be an Intrigue unless specified. Secrets' steal icon takes one Intrigue selected at random from each opponent who has 4 or more Intrigues.
observed.evidence: Discarding; Intrigue cards: Steal Intrigue icon.

grades.reason: Each limits ordinary discard to hand/non-Intrigue unless specified and gives random theft from every opponent with four-plus; Secrets' other effects are unasked.

grades.question: Which cards may a trash effect remove, where do ordinary and Reserve cards go, and is trashing optional? Does trashing The Spice Must Flow remove its acquired VP?
grades.expected: May trash own hand, discard or in-play card. Ordinary to box; Reserve back to its Reserve stack. Optional unless cost or direct self-trash. The Spice Must Flow acquire VP retained after trashing.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1185–1190; FAQ p4 The Spice Must Flow

observed.evidence: Trashing; FAQ & Rulings: Victory.

grades.reason: Each covers hand/discard/in-play trash, box versus Reserve destinations, optionality exceptions and retained Spice Must Flow VP.

grades.question: When do acquire-box effects resolve, when do you reshuffle your deck, and can unused Persuasion be carried to another round?
grades.expected: Acquire effect once at acquisition not when later played. Reshuffle discard only when unable to draw due to empty deck then continue. Unspent Reveal Persuasion lost, never saved.

grades.question: What counts as in play for Fremen Bond, can two Bond cards activate one another regardless of play order, and when do they cease being in play?
grades.expected: Agent-turn and Reveal cards remain in play face up until Reveal Clean Up unless trashed earlier. Bond requires at least one other Fremen in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of order.

observed.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed during Reveal remain face up and in play until Clean Up, unless trashed first. A Fremen Bond effect works if one or more other Fremen cards are in play; two Bond cards can activate one another regardless of order. They cease being in play at Clean Up when moved to discard.
observed.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond.

grades.reason: Each defines Agent/Reveal in-play lifetime, other-Fremen condition, reciprocal Bond activation independent of order and Clean Up/early trash ending.

grades.question: Can Recall Agent return the Agent placed this turn, and when can the recalled Agent act again? Where does a retreated troop go, and may “retreat any number” mean zero?
grades.expected: Recall another Agent from board to Leader, not current-turn Agent; can use on later Agent turn same round. Retreat Conflict to garrison; any number permits zero.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1147–1157; FAQ p3 Retreat

observed.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent sent this turn; it can be used again on a later Agent turn in that round. A retreated troop goes from Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” permits zero.
observed.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ Combat and troops.

grades.reason: Each excludes the just-placed Agent, permits later same-round reuse, retreats troops to garrison and allows zero retreats.

grades.question: When an effect grants two Influence with a freely chosen Faction, may it be split? What is required for an Alliance-icon effect or a minimum-Influence effect?
grades.expected: Choose one Faction, both Influence there (not split). Alliance effect requires holding shown Faction Alliance token; minimum-Influence effect requires at least shown value with shown Faction.

observed.answer: A free-choice effect that gains two Influence must put both with one chosen Faction; it cannot split them. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction's Alliance token. A minimum-Influence effect requires the stated minimum with its named Faction.
observed.evidence: Influence: gain two free choice cannot choose different Factions; Alliance and minimum Influence requirements.

grades.reason: Each keeps both Influence in one chosen Faction and states Alliance ownership and named minimum-Influence eligibility.

grades.question: If an Alliance holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, who receives the token? If the holder drops to 3 and no one has 4, what happens?
grades.expected: Former holder chooses one of previously tied opponents to receive token; holder loses Alliance VP and receiver gains it. Below 4 loses token; if no eligible 4+ player return token to board, losing its VP.

observed.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, the former holder chooses which of the previously tied opponents receives the Alliance. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the token to the board; the former holder loses its 1 VP.
observed.evidence: Victory Points / Alliance loss FAQ.

grades.reason: Each assigns choice among formerly tied opponents to the losing holder and returns token to board with lost VP if nobody remains at four-plus.

grades.question: What happens to a card drawn during Reveal compared with one drawn after Reveal? What happens to a Plot Intrigue played earlier whose effect applies at Reveal?
grades.expected: During Reveal immediately reveal and use this turn; after Reveal keep until next round, then draw five extra. Plot effect for later Reveal stays face up until that Reveal, use then discard.

observed.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the normal five-card draw. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up until then, is used, and then discarded.
observed.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Draw timing.

grades.reason: Each reveals/uses a during-Reveal draw now, keeps an after-Reveal draw in addition to next five and preserves delayed Plot face up until resolution/discard.

grades.question: May a “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue be played after tying for first? What if you receive such an Intrigue as a reward for an outright win?
grades.expected: Tie for first is not a win, cannot play. An appropriate Intrigue received as winning reward can be played immediately.
grades.source_references: FAQ p4 When you win a Conflict

observed.answer: No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because nobody wins. If you receive one as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
observed.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Combat and troops.

grades.reason: Each rejects a tied-first win trigger and permits immediate play when received as an outright-win reward.

grades.question: What if final VP, spice, Solari, water and garrison troops all remain tied, and may scores exceed 12?
grades.expected: Final tiebreaker is player who most recently took Reveal turn. Scores may exceed printed track maximum 12.
grades.source_references: FAQ p2 Endgame; p4 Victory Points

observed.answer: If all resource tiebreakers also tie, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed track's 12.
observed.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Victory.

grades.reason: Each uses most recent Reveal as final tiebreaker and permits scores above twelve.

grades.question: Can you delay completion of two held contracts for the same board space after visiting, and when in the Agent turn can their effects resolve?
grades.expected: Completion mandatory; all same-space contracts completed with one Agent placement. Their effects may resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects; still must hold them at placement.

observed.answer: No. All contracts held for the same space must be fulfilled with one Agent placement; you cannot delay them. Contract effects are another effect of that Agent turn and may resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects, provided you held each contract when sending the Agent.
observed.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Contract completion is mandatory.

grades.reason: Each mandates all held same-space contracts on one placement, permits ordering with card/space effects and preserves ownership-at-placement condition.

grades.question: Under CHOAM does Shaddam begin with his set-aside Sardaukar contracts, when can he take one, and how long does his Signet Ring deployment restriction last?
grades.expected: No, not in possession at start. Sardaukar Commander allows acquiring set-aside Sardaukar contract instead of generally available one when taking a contract. Emperor of Known Universe restriction starts immediately with Signet Ring Agent placement and lasts that turn only.
grades.source_references: Main p17; FAQ p3 Shaddam Corrino IV

observed.answer: No, Shaddam does not start with the two reserved Sardaukar contracts; he may choose one instead of a generally available one when acquiring a contract, and only Shaddam may take them. His Signet Ring deployment restriction applies immediately on the Agent turn when he plays Signet Ring and lasts for that turn only.
observed.evidence: CHOAM setup; Reserved Sardaukar contracts; Shaddam's Signet benefits; FAQ Shaddam.

grades.reason: Each distinguishes reserved contracts from starting possession, allows Shaddam's substitution when acquiring and starts the deployment restriction immediately for that turn.

grades.question: For Feyd, where does the Training token start and what happens at its last space? Which Jessica side begins face up and can Reverend Mother Jessica act on the flip turn?
grades.expected: Feyd starts leftmost Training space, stays forever on rightmost once reached. Lady Jessica side starts up, not Reverend Mother. Reverend Mother ability usable on flip turn.
grades.source_references: Main p17 / extraction 957–964; FAQ p3 Reverend Mother Jessica

observed.answer: Feyd's token starts on the leftmost Training-track space and stays on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica begins face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
observed.evidence: Leader clarifications; FAQ & Rulings.

grades.reason: Each gives Feyd's leftmost start/rightmost permanence, Lady Jessica starting face and Reverend Mother's same-turn flip use.

grades.question: For Margot and Irulan does moving from 1 to 3 Influence count as reaching 2, can it trigger again later, and does descending through 2 count? Does Clean Up trigger Spacing Guild’s Favor discard ability?
grades.expected: Passing 2 upward counts, can repeat by losing then regaining Influence; descending does not count. Spacing Guild Favor triggers discard from hand, not in-play-to-discard Clean Up.

observed.answer: Yes, moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2, and reaching 2 with the same Faction may trigger again after losing Influence and later moving up to 2; moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding from hand does.
observed.evidence: Leader clarifications: Margot/Irulan and Spacing Guild's Favor.

grades.reason: Each counts upward passing two, permits later retrigger, excludes descending and restricts Favor's discard trigger to hand rather than Clean Up.

grades.question: State Accept Contract and Dutiful Service’s Agent icons and effects with and without CHOAM, and whether both automatically advance a Faction track.
grades.expected: Accept Contract: Spice Trade, draw card plus contract or 2 Solari, no automatic Faction Influence. Dutiful Service: Emperor, one Emperor Influence plus contract or 2 Solari. Contract fallback if module off or all contracts taken.

observed.answer: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade icon, is not a Faction, and always draws one card; its contract icon gives 2 Solari without CHOAM, takes/replaces a contract when CHOAM has contracts available, and gives 2 Solari when all are taken. It gives no automatic Influence. Dutiful Service uses the Emperor icon, gives 1 Emperor Influence total (automatically as an Emperor space), and resolves that same contract-icon rule; it does not grant a second Emperor advance beyond the one listed.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: contract spaces and Faction status table.

grades.reason: Each distinguishes Spice Trade Accept Contract's draw/no Influence from Emperor Dutiful Service's single advance and applies both CHOAM/fallback states.

grades.question: What do Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station each cost and provide, what Agent icons access them, and which are Combat spaces?
grades.expected: Arrakeen City free, troop and card, controller 1 Solari. Fremkit Fremen free, 1 Fremen Influence and card. Research Station City 2 water, two troops and two cards. All Combat.

observed.answer: Arrakeen: City, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits 1 troop and draws 1 card, while controller gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw 1 card. Research Station: City, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit 2 troops and draw 2 cards.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide table.

grades.reason: Each gives all three access icons, costs, exact effects including Arrakeen controller income and Combat status.

grades.question: Compare Deep Desert and Hagga Basin’s entry costs, base spice and worm choices. Do you still collect bonus spice when choosing worms, and are Hooks spent?
grades.expected: Deep Desert 3 water, 4 spice OR two worms; Hagga 1 water, 2 spice OR one worm. Both collect all bonus spice even with worms. Worm choice requires Maker Hooks, not spent; cannot summon into Shield-Wall-protected Conflict.
grades.source_references: Supplements pp1–2; Main p10; FAQ p2 Maker hooks

observed.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water; choose 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, summon 2 sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water; choose 2 base spice or, with Hooks, summon 1 sandworm. Both choices also collect all bonus spice there. Hooks are not spent when summoning.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: Deep Desert and Hagga Basin; Sandworms; FAQ Spies.

grades.reason: Each gives the two water costs and exclusive base-spice/worm quantities, preserves all bonus spice on either branch and retains Hooks.

grades.question: For each Sietch Tabr option, state requirements and effects. Do you get a troop when choosing to remove the Shield Wall?
grades.expected: City access, 2+ Fremen Influence, no resource cost. Option one Hooks if needed, one troop, one water; option two one water and may remove wall. Option two gives no troop or Hooks. Combat space.

observed.answer: Both options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit 1 troop, and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second option gives no troop.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: Sietch Tabr.

grades.reason: Each gives City/2+ Fremen/no resource cost for both options, exact branch rewards and no troop on Wall removal.

grades.question: How do High Council’s first and subsequent visits differ, what does each cost, when is its ongoing benefit used, and is it a Combat space?
grades.expected: Landsraad 5 Solari each visit. First Councilor to empty seat, +2 Persuasion each Reveal rest of game; later 2 spice, Intrigue, three troops. Not Combat, cannot normally deploy recruited troops.

observed.answer: High Council uses Landsraad access, is not a Combat space, and costs 5 Solari each visit. On your first visit, place your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Later visits gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit 3 troops.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: High Council.

grades.reason: Each specifies five Solari on each visit, first Councilor placement and every-Reveal two Persuasion, later spice/Intrigue/three troops and noncombat status.

grades.question: What does Swordmaster cost before and after anyone obtains one, how often may each player visit, and when can the new Agent be used? Does a Rival obtaining it lower human cost?
grades.expected: Landsraad 8 Solari before any Swordmaster, then 6; once per player per game. Third Agent from beside board onto Leader immediately usable same round and rest of game. Rival also lowers cost.

observed.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone has one and 6 after anyone obtains one; it is once per player per game. Take the third Agent from beside the board to your Leader, available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining Swordmaster also reduces the human cost to 6.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: Swordmaster.

grades.reason: Each gives eight/six costs with Rival-triggered discount, once-per-player limit and third Agent immediately available this round/rest of game.

grades.question: State Imperial Privilege’s Agent icon, requirement, entry cost and effects. Which Agent can it recall and does it automatically give Emperor Influence?
grades.expected: Landsraad, 2+ Emperor Influence, 3 Solari. May discard Intrigue to draw Intrigue; recall another Agent and draw card. Not the current Agent. No automatic Emperor Influence.

observed.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access, requires 2+ Emperor Influence, costs 3 Solari, and is not a Combat space. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, recall one of your other Agents, and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Privilege; Recall Agent icon.

grades.reason: Each gives Landsraad, two Emperor Influence, three Solari, Intrigue exchange, recall of another Agent/card draw and no automatic Emperor advance.

grades.question: State Shipping’s access icon, Influence requirement, cost and gains. Does its free-choice Influence have to be with the Guild?
grades.expected: Spice Trade, 2+ Guild Influence, 3 spice. Gain 5 Solari and one Influence any one Faction, not necessarily Guild.

observed.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Guild Influence, costs 3 spice, and is not a Combat space. It gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; the free-choice Influence need not be Guild.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: Shipping.

grades.reason: Each gives Spice Trade, two Guild Influence, three spice, five Solari and unrestricted choice of one Faction Influence.

grades.question: Compare Gather Support and Spice Refinery’s zero-cost and paid options and Combat status.
grades.expected: Gather Support Landsraad choose 0/2 Solari, two troops either way, plus one water if paid, not Combat. Refinery City choose 0/1 spice, gain 2/4 Solari respectively, controller 1 Solari either way, Combat.

observed.answer: Gather Support uses Landsraad access, is not Combat, and lets you choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari: recruit 2 troops either way, and gain 1 water if you paid 2. Spice Refinery uses City access, is Combat; choose to pay 0 or 1 spice, gaining 2 Solari or 4 Solari if you pay 1. Its controller also gains 1 Solari on any visit.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide table.

grades.reason: Each gives both costs and branch rewards for each space, controller income and differing Combat status.

grades.question: State Heighliner, Desert Tactics and Sardaukar’s entry costs, Influence gains, recruits and other effects; which allow normal deployment?
grades.expected: Heighliner 5 spice, Guild Influence +1 and five troops, Combat. Desert Tactics 1 water, Fremen Influence +1 and one troop, optional trash, Combat. Sardaukar 4 spice, Emperor Influence +1 and four troops plus Intrigue, not Combat.

Desert Tactics: Fremen, Combat yes, costs 1 water; gain 1 Fremen Influence, recruit 1 troop, optionally trash a card. Sardaukar: Emperor, Combat no, costs 4 spice; gain 1 Emperor Influence, draw an Intrigue, recruit 4 troops.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide table.

grades.reason: Each states the exact costs, Faction gains, recruit quantities and other effects for all three, allowing deployment only at Heighliner/Desert Tactics.

grades.question: What are Assembly Hall, Espionage and Deliver Supplies’s Agent icons, costs and effects, including Assembly Hall’s timing condition?
grades.expected: Assembly Hall Landsraad free, Intrigue now, 1 Persuasion at Reveal if own Agent there. Espionage BG 1 spice, 1 BG Influence, card and Spy. Deliver Supplies Guild free, 1 Guild Influence and 1 water. None Combat.

observed.answer: Assembly Hall uses Landsraad access, costs nothing, is not Combat; draw an Intrigue, and gain 1 Persuasion during Reveal if your Agent is there. Espionage uses Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, is not Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card, place a Spy. Deliver Supplies uses Spacing Guild, costs nothing, is not Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide table.

grades.reason: Each specifies all three icons/costs/effects and Assembly Hall's own-Agent-at-Reveal condition.

grades.question: What must False Orders’ affected opponents do, may it be played without an opposing Spy connected to your destination, and when is Litany Against Fear’s red box ignored?
grades.expected: Each affected opponent moves Spy to empty observation post not connected to this turn Agent destination. Can play without enemy Spy there. Litany red box ignored during Reveal or with gained Agent icon when played normally as Agent card.
grades.source_references: FAQ pp2–3 False Orders/Litany Against Fear

observed.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn; it can be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
observed.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: False Orders; Litany Against Fear.

grades.reason: Each gives False Orders' empty nonconnected-post move and permissive play with no target Spy, plus both Litany red-box exceptions.

grades.question: With Manipulate, may opponents acquire the removed card, may you acquire it by other means with the discount, and when does an unacquired card leave the game?
grades.expected: Opponents cannot acquire. You may use other means but 1-Persuasion discount does not apply. If not acquired by end of next Reveal turn, remove from game.

observed.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it has not been acquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
observed.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Manipulate.

grades.reason: Each excludes opponents, permits own other acquisition without discount and removes the card at end of next Reveal if unacquired.

grades.question: What components and resource does the standard two-player Rival start with, what happens to the 2P Reshuffle card, and can its 10 VP trigger Endgame and victory?
grades.expected: Four cubes at Influence bottoms, three garrison troops rest supply, two Agents supply and third beside board, three Spies and one water supply, score/Combat zero. Retain Reshuffle in Hagal. Scoring Rival can trigger end at 10+ and win.

observed.answer: The Rival starts with four cubes on the bottom Influence spaces, 3 troops in its garrison and remaining troops in supply, 2 Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board, 3 Spies, 1 water, and score and Combat markers at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and place it near the Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. Its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall just like a human's score, and it can win.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup; Rival can win.

grades.reason: Each gives all Rival setup components/locations and markers, retains 2P Reshuffle and allows a Recall end trigger/win.

grades.question: When does a Rival buy Swordmaster, how does it count and prioritize spending resources, does it keep leftovers, and is its Agent available immediately?
grades.expected: As soon as total resources reaches printed value; Solari spice Intrigues water each unit one. Spend only threshold, prioritizing Solari then spice then Intrigue then water; keep leftovers. Third Agent immediately available including current round.
grades.source_references: Supplements p5; p2 Swordmaster; FAQ p3 Rivals

observed.answer: As soon as its Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, and water total reaches its printed Swordmaster value, it spends exactly that many resources and takes its third Agent, available in the current round. It counts each unit/card as one and must spend Solari first, then spice, Intrigue cards, then water, using as much of each type as needed. It keeps all leftovers and cannot choose a different mix to save higher-priority resources.
observed.evidence: Swordmaster resource total; spending priority is mandatory.

grades.reason: Each counts all four resource types one-for-one, buys immediately at threshold, spends exactly the price in mandatory order, keeps leftovers and uses Agent now.

grades.question: After a Rival has Swordmaster, which exact resource sets does it spend for VP, and can it spend a mixed total of seven resources for a VP?
grades.expected: Each set 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigues or 3 water gives 1 VP whenever available. No mixed seven-resource VP purchase; mixed total only used for Swordmaster.
grades.source_references: Supplements p5 Buying Victory Points diagram

observed.answer: After Swordmaster, the Rival spends each set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP. It cannot combine a mixed total of seven resources for a VP.
observed.evidence: After Swordmaster: whenever Rival has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue, or 3 water, spend each such set for 1 VP.

grades.reason: Each lists homogeneous seven Solari/seven spice/three Intrigue/three water conversions and rejects mixed-resource VP payment.

grades.question: When choosing Influence, how does a Rival select the Faction and break ties? Does it get VP at 2 and Alliance VP, or the track bonus at 4? What does a numbered Hagal Influence icon mean?
grades.expected: Choose least Influence, ties leftmost priority. Gains/losses of Influence VP and Alliance VP as humans, no 4-track bonus. Number means Faction at that position in printed priority list.

observed.answer: The Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by the leftmost Faction in its priority list; numbered Hagal Influence icons refer to positions in that priority list. It gets the ordinary 1 VP at 2 Influence and an Alliance token's 1 VP if it holds it. At 4 Influence it does not receive the track bonus resource.
observed.evidence: Victory Points: Faction Influence; After Swordmaster; Rival Combat: Influence choice; Hagal numbered Influence.

grades.reason: Each uses least Influence then leftmost priority, preserves human-like threshold/Alliance VP, excludes four-track resources and interprets numbered priority icons.

grades.question: A Rival reveals a two-destination Hagal card and the condition-selected destination is occupied. Can it use the other destination, and what conditions select these cards?
grades.expected: Cannot switch to other; reveal again. Accept Contract/Shipping based on Guild Influence; Deliver Supplies/Heighliner based on Conflict tier I/II/III. Use card printed condition.
grades.source_references: Supplements p4 Special Instructions; FAQ p3 Rivals

observed.answer: No. Use only the destination matching current conditions; if it is occupied, reveal a new Hagal card and do not use the other destination. Guild Influence selects Accept Contract or Shipping; Conflict tier selects Deliver Supplies or Heighliner.
observed.evidence: Rival Agent turns: two-destination card conditions and occupied destination.

grades.reason: Each redraws rather than switching destinations and identifies Guild Influence versus Conflict tier as the card conditions.

grades.question: A Rival has no troops newly recruited by a card sending it to Combat. Can it deploy garrison troops? What if a Hagal card recruits at a noncombat space or has a conditional 2-Influence bonus not met?
grades.expected: Still deploy up to two available garrison troops at Combat. New troops at noncombat go garrison. Missing 2-Influence bonus does not block placement, just no bonus. Use only Hagal effects, not ordinary board effects.

observed.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to 2 available garrison troops even if the card recruited none; newly recruited troops also deploy there. At a noncombat space, recruited troops go in its garrison. If it lacks 2+ Influence for a conditional bonus, that bonus is omitted but does not prevent placing the Agent.
observed.evidence: Rival Agent turns: troop icons and conditional bonuses.

grades.reason: Each deploys up to two older garrison troops despite no recruits, sends noncombat recruits to garrison and omits an unmet bonus without blocking placement.

grades.question: How does a Rival choose an unrestricted Spy post, what happens if all Faction posts are occupied, and what occurs on placing its third Spy? Can it Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence?
grades.expected: First available Faction post by priority; if all full ignore placement. Third/final supply Spy placed triggers immediately recalling other two and printed Scheme. Never Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence.

observed.answer: Unless a post type is specified, the Rival uses the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy recalls its other two Spies and triggers its Scheme. The Rival never recalls Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
observed.evidence: Spies and Schemes.

grades.reason: Each places unrestricted Spies by Faction priority, ignores full posts, recalls the other two on the third placement for Scheme and never uses human Spy recalls.

grades.question: If a Rival’s Scheme recruits troops before a Hagal Agent reaches a Combat space on that same turn, what happens to those troops? What if a Place Spy card found no legal post?
grades.expected: Deploy Scheme recruits on same-turn Combat placement. Place Spy card still followed by another Hagal reveal whether placement succeeds or not, because no Agent has been sent.

observed.answer: If the Scheme recruits troops before the Rival visits a Combat space that turn, those newly recruited troops deploy there too. If a Place Spy card finds no legal empty post, ignore placement and immediately reveal another Hagal card because the card has not sent an Agent.
observed.evidence: Spies and Schemes; Place Spy cards do not place an Agent.

grades.reason: Each includes Scheme recruits in the same-turn Combat deployment and redraws after a failed Place Spy because no Agent was placed.

grades.question: At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, how does a Rival choose worms versus base spice with Hooks, without Hooks, or with a protected Conflict? What happens to accumulated bonus spice?
grades.expected: Always take bonus spice. With Hooks and summonable Conflict summons one at Hagga/two Deep instead of base. Without Hooks or if protected, summons none and gains base spice (2/4). At Imperial Basin gains base1. Hagal wall removal requires Hooks.

observed.answer: At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, the Rival collects all bonus spice. With its own Hooks and a Conflict that allows worms, it summons one worm at Hagga or two at Deep Desert instead of taking base spice. If it summons none, it takes base spice (2 at Hagga, 4 at Deep Desert); without Hooks or when Shield Wall protects that Conflict, it cannot summon. Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice. Hooks remain on its garrison.
observed.evidence: Maker spaces: Rival; Hooks and Wall icons; board-space table.

grades.reason: Each always takes bonus spice, summons one/two instead of base when Hooks and Conflict permit, otherwise takes two/four base spice.

grades.question: When and how is a Rival’s Combat strength bonus determined, what if Reshuffle appears, and can humans respond afterward? Does a unit-free Rival get this bonus?
grades.expected: Start Combat in turn order, only with deployed unit: one Hagal card, bottom swords only added. Reshuffle and draw again on Reshuffle. Humans then Combat Intrigue before resolution. No unit no bonus.

observed.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal a Hagal card in turn order and add its bottom swords as strength; if Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Then humans have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A unit-free Rival does not get this bonus.
observed.evidence: Combat: Rival.

grades.reason: Each grants only a deployed-unit Rival its start-of-Combat bottom-sword draw, handles Reshuffle by redrawing and leaves humans their following response window.

grades.question: Can a Rival gain control, defensive troops, battle-icon VP and doubled rewards? How does it handle optional Conflict VP payments and contract rewards with CHOAM?
grades.expected: Normal control visit bonus and defensive supply troop; win card/match icons; sandworms double. Always buy optional Conflict VP if can pay resources or required Spy recall. Never contracts; each contract reward becomes 2 Solari even with CHOAM.

observed.answer: Yes. The Rival receives normal rewards, doubles them with one or more sandworms, wins Conflict cards and battle-icon VP normally, gains control bonuses on visits and defensive troops when its controlled Conflict is revealed. It always takes optional Conflict VP if it can pay or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
observed.evidence: Combat: Rival.

grades.reason: Each grants normal control/defense, battle-icon and sandworm reward benefits, mandates affordable optional VP and substitutes two Solari for contracts even with CHOAM.

grades.question: When during Reveal do you total, announce and set Combat strength, can you update it during the turn, and how is strength over 20 marked?
grades.expected: After Reveal Cards and before Clean Up, at any point while resolving effects; announce total, set marker and update as needed. Above20 flip +20 side and count again from beginning of track.

observed.answer: During Reveal effects, total and announce strength and set the Combat marker at any point; update it as needed while resolving the turn. If strength exceeds 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
observed.evidence: Reveal Turn; Strength.

grades.reason: Each totals/announces/sets and updates during Reveal effect resolution and uses the +20 marker side with track restart above twenty.

grades.question: When is a Leader’s Signet Ring ability activated, does merely revealing Signet Ring activate it, and can card text override normal game rules?
grades.expected: Activated when playing Signet Ring on an Agent turn, not when merely revealing. Left Leader ability used as described. Cards of any type can override normal rules.

observed.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when you reveal the card. Cards of any type can override the usual rules of the game.
observed.evidence: Setup Leader abilities; Overview: cards of any type can override usual rules.
